title: Crutch Comments Covering Bad Names
pattern: Comments written primarily to explain what an ambiguous or misleading variable/function name actually means.
why_bad: Fails to address the root defect. A good name is always superior to a comment. Instead of fixing the obscure name, the developer uses prose to bridge the readability gap, creating double maintenance overhead.
detection: Functions or variables with vague names (like `clean`, `process`, `handle`) preceded by comments detailing the precise limit or business logic being checked.
counterexample: A self-descriptive name that eliminates the need for the comment: `fn enforce_response_byte_limit(reply: &mut Response)`.
fix: Rename the function or variable to reflect its true semantic intent; remove the comment.
source: Dustin Boswell & Trevor Foucher, *The Art of Readable Code* (2012), Chapter 5 ("Don't Comment Bad Names - Fix the Names Instead").
